title: Are you doing your homework?
grammar: Present continuous: yes/no questions and short answers
vocab_topic: Homework, school subjects and activities at home
pair_game: Point at a picture. Ask: “Are you doing your …?” Your partner answers. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: Are you …? Yes, I am.
rows: Yes, I am. / No, I am not.
Yes, he is. / No, she is not.
grammar_box.tip: Short answers: Yes, I am. (NOT Yes, I am doing.)

questions: Are you doing your homework right now?
What are you doing after school today?
Where do you usually do your homework?
Do you like doing homework? Why?
Are your parents helping you with homework?
What subject are you studying today?
Is it easy or hard to do homework at home?
What are your friends doing now?
Do you watch TV after you finish homework?
Who checks your homework at home?
starters: Yes, I am. / No, I am not. I am … .
I usually do my homework in the … .
I like / do not like homework because … .
Yes, they are. / No, they are not. My … helps me.
Yes, I do. / No, I do not. First I … .
samples: Are you doing your homework right now?
No, I **am not**. I **am talking** to my friend. I do my homework after dinner.
Where do you usually do your homework?
I usually do it in the kitchen. My bedroom is cold, and the kitchen is warm.
Who checks your homework at home?
My mother checks my maths and my big brother checks my English. He is very good at English.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: Where do you do your homework?

game.title: Find someone who…
game.rules: Walk around the class. Ask: “Are you …?” or “Do you …?” Write a name.

mini_talk.title: My homework time
plan: Say when you do your homework
mini_talk.model: I do my homework at five o'clock, right after my snack. I do it in the kitchen because my bedroom is cold and the kitchen is warm. My mother **is helping** me with maths today, because it is difficult. After my homework I watch TV or I play football outside with my friends.

say who helps me at home
